R1.q: ___ you got any idea where Marco is?
R1.e: 'Have got' makes questions by inverting have: Have you got…? We don't use do/did with 'have got'.

R1.q: Sara is so ___ – she remembers everyone's birthday and always asks how you are.
R1.e: Considerate people think about other people's feelings and needs.

R1.q: ___ the rain, the match went ahead as planned.
R1.e: Despite + noun. 'In spite' needs 'of', and 'although' needs a full clause (although it rained).

R1.q: He was ___ from his job after he was caught stealing.
R1.e: Be sacked = lose your job because your employer ends it. Resign means you choose to leave; hired is the opposite of sacked.

R1.q: When I was little, my grandfather ___ take me fishing every Sunday.
R1.e: Would + infinitive describes repeated actions in the past. 'Used' would need 'to': used to take.

R1.q: As a teenager I suffered from terrible ___ (shy).
R1.e: Add -ness to many adjectives to make abstract nouns: shy → shyness, kind → kindness.

R1.q: The children made the decorations ___; nobody helped them.
R1.e: Reflexive pronoun for emphasis: they did it themselves, without help. 'Theirselves' doesn't exist.

R1.q: Words like 'kid' and 'telly' are informal; in an essay you should use more ___ words.
R1.e: Essays need formal language. Slang and colloquial words are informal; jargon is specialist language.

R1.q: We got ___ in the traffic and missed the start of the film.
R1.e: Get + past participle describes a change of state: get stuck, get lost. 'Stuck' is the participle of stick.

R1.q: The weather was awful. ___, we had a great time.
R1.e: Nevertheless introduces a contrast: something is true even though the first sentence suggests it might not be.

R1.q: After three days of fighting, the soldiers were forced to s___ to the enemy.
R1.e: Surrender = stop fighting and accept that the enemy has won.

R1.q: It's hard to get your message a___ when everyone is talking at once.
R1.e: Get something across = make people understand an idea or message.

R1.q: I went to bed early s___ as to be fresh for the interview.
R1.e: So as to + infinitive expresses purpose, like 'in order to'.

R1.q: I ___ (not / use to) like olives, but now I love them.
R1.e: Negative of used to: didn't use to (no -d after 'did').

R1.q: I ___ my keys twice last week.
R1.e: For specific incidents that happened a certain number of times, use the past simple, not would or used to.

R2.e: After a negative adverb like 'never' at the start, we invert the subject and auxiliary: never have I seen.

R2.q: Not only ___ the exam, but she got the highest mark in the class.
R2.e: Not only + inversion. In the past simple we add did: not only did she pass.

R2.q: The film is set in Sicily in the 1950s, and the ___ is full of surprising twists.
R2.e: The plot is the story of a book or film. Twists are unexpected changes in the plot.

R2.q: I couldn't put the book down – it was a real p___-turner.
R2.e: A page-turner is a book so exciting that you want to keep reading.

R2.q: He ___ have left already – his car isn't outside.
R2.e: Must have + past participle = we're almost sure something happened, because of the evidence (no car).

R2.q: She ___ have seen you – she would have said hello.
R2.e: Can't have + past participle = we're sure something didn't happen.

R2.q: The old door ___ loudly as it opened slowly in the wind.
R2.e: Creak = make a long, high sound, like an old door or wooden floor.

R2.q: She had a sore throat, so she could only speak in a w___.
R2.e: A whisper is a very quiet way of speaking, using your breath and not your voice.
Be reported + perfect infinitive (to have + past participle) for a past event. It distances the speaker from the fact.

R2.q: ___ that the museum will close for repairs.
R2.e: It + passive reporting verb + that (It is expected that…) shows the information isn't the speaker's own.

R2.q: I'm running ___ of time – can we talk later?
R2.e: Run out of time = have no time left.

R2.q: It's only a m___ of time before someone finds out.
R2.e: It's only a matter of time = it will certainly happen soon.

R2.q: It's time we ___ home – it's getting late.
R2.e: It's time + subject + past simple to say something should happen now. The meaning is present.

R2.q: I'd rather you ___ (not tell) anyone about this.
R2.e: I'd rather + another person + past simple to talk about the present or future.

R2.q: I bought my scooter in ___, paying fifty euros a month.
R2.e: Pay in instalments = pay a fixed amount regularly until you have paid the full price.

R3.q: My parents never let me ___ out late on school nights.
R3.e: Let + object + infinitive without to: let me stay. Make works the same way.

R3.q: I can't imagine him ___ up at six every day.
R3.e: Imagine + object + -ing: I can't imagine him getting up.

R3.q: He's so ___ that he forgets where he's parked his car almost every day.
R3.e: Absent-minded = often forgetting things because you are thinking about something else.

R3.q: ___ you need any help, just give me a call.
R3.e: Should + subject at the start of a conditional = if. It's a slightly more formal way to say 'if you need'.

R3.q: If I ___ (know) you were coming, I'd have made a cake.
R3.e: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle, for an imaginary past situation.

R3.q: My little brother is completely addicted ___ his tablet.
R3.e: The adjective 'addicted' is followed by 'to': addicted to something.

R3.q: You ___ to use your phone during the exam – put it in your bag.
R3.e: Not be allowed to = it isn't permitted. Mustn't, can't and needn't are followed by the infinitive without to.

R3.q: The shop ___ (charge) me – I paid twenty euros for a ten-euro T-shirt!
R3.e: The prefix over- means too much: overcharge = ask someone to pay too much.

R3.q: The soup ___ delicious – what's in it?
R3.e: Smell + adjective. Use 'smell like' + noun. Verbs of perception like this are usually not continuous.

R3.q: I only see my cousins once in a b___ moon.
R3.e: Once in a blue moon = very rarely.

R3.q: I remember ___ taken to the beach as a small child.
R3.e: Remember + -ing for memories of the past. Being taken is the passive gerund: someone took me.

R3.q: After the long walk I slept like a l___.
R3.e: Sleep like a log = sleep very deeply. It's a simile, a comparison with 'like'.

R3.q: The concert is ___ the point of starting.
R3.e: Be on the point of + -ing = be going to do something very soon.

R3.q: Positano is lovely, but in August it's full of tourists and very ___.
R3.e: Touristy = full of tourists and things made for them. It's often slightly negative.

R3.q: We decided to go on a guided t___ of the old town.
R3.e: A guided tour = a visit to a place with a guide who explains things.

R4.q: I didn't want to go, but I had ___.
R4.e: We can leave out the verb after 'to' if it's clear: I had to (go).

R4.q: She can speak Arabic, and so ___ her brother.
R4.e: So + auxiliary + subject. Repeat the same auxiliary as the first verb: she can… so can he.

R4.q: Our dog ___ his tail whenever he sees us.
R4.e: Dogs wag their tails (move them from side to side) when they are happy.

R4.q: Many people refuse to buy products that were tested on animals because they think it's c___.
R4.e: Cruel = causing pain or suffering on purpose.
Compound noun: the first noun works like an adjective and says what type (a knife for bread).

R4.q: We're meeting at my ___ (parents) house on Sunday.
R4.e: For a plural noun ending in -s, add only an apostrophe: my parents' house.

R4.q: ___ the onions finely before adding them to the pan.
R4.e: Chop = cut into small pieces with a knife.

R4.q: The woman ___ I spoke to on the phone was very helpful.
R4.e: Whom is the object form of who. It's formal, but correct: the woman (whom) I spoke to.

R4.q: The stadium, ___ was built in 1932, is being renovated.
R4.e: Non-defining relative clauses (with commas) use which for things. We can't use that here.
The noun from determined is determination (-ation ending).

R4.q: What annoys me ___ the way he interrupts everyone.
R4.e: In a cleft sentence with 'What…', the verb is usually singular: What annoys me is…

R4.q: It ___ (be) my brother who broke the window, not me.
R4.e: Cleft sentence: It + be + the important part + who/that… It's past, so use was.

R4.q: Can you ___ me what time the museum opens?
R4.e: Tell + person + information. Say and explain don't take a person directly after them.

R4.q: Don't forget to b___ your umbrella when you come to my house.
R4.e: Bring = carry something to where the speaker is. Take = carry it away from here.

R4.q: His advice had a big ___ on my decision.
R4.e: Effect is a noun (have an effect on). Affect is usually a verb.

T1.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Do you have got any brothers?
T1.e: Questions with 'have got' invert have and the subject. Possession isn't used in the continuous.

T1.q: Did you ___ a good time in London?
T1.e: After did, use the base form: did you have. 'Have got' isn't used for experiences like 'have a good time'.

T1.q: Lucia is very ___; she hates spending money, even on her friends.
T1.e: Mean = not wanting to spend or share money. Generous is the opposite.

T1.q: Someone who is ___ refuses to change their mind, even when they're clearly wrong.
T1.e: Stubborn = not willing to change your opinion or behaviour.

T1.q: My grandfather is very n___; he always wants to know everyone's business.
T1.e: Nosy = too interested in other people's private lives.

T1.q: I took a taxi ___ miss the train.
T1.e: So as not to + infinitive = negative purpose. 'In order not' would need 'to'.

T1.q: ___ his age, he runs ten kilometres every morning.
T1.e: Despite + noun (his age). Although and even though need a clause with a verb.

T1.q: After twenty years with the company, he was ___ to manager.
T1.e: Be promoted = be given a more important job in the same company.

T1.q: The factory closed and three hundred workers were made r___.
T1.e: Be made redundant = lose your job because the company doesn't need you any more.

T1.q: We should leave now; o___, we'll be late.
T1.e: Otherwise = if not. It shows the result if something doesn't happen.

T1.q: Every summer we ___ to my aunt's house in Cefalù.
T1.e: Would + infinitive for repeated past habits. 'Use to' needs a -d in positive sentences: used to go.

T1.q: I ___ my phone on the bus yesterday.
T1.e: A single, specific past event needs the past simple, not would or used to.

T1.q: My dad ___ always telling us to switch off the lights.
T1.e: Past continuous + always describes a repeated, often annoying, past habit.

T1.q: The ___ of the city at night took my breath away.
T1.e: We need a noun after 'the … of'. Beauty is the abstract noun from beautiful.

T1.q: Children need love and ___ (free) to grow up happy.
T1.e: The suffix -dom makes abstract nouns: free → freedom, bored → boredom.

T1.q: Did you enjoy ___ at the party?
T1.e: Enjoy yourself = have a good time. Enjoy needs an object, here a reflexive pronoun.

T1.q: ___ has to bring something to eat; it's a shared lunch.
T1.e: Everyone is a pronoun and takes a singular verb (has). Every must be followed by a noun.

T1.q: People from different parts of Sicily have slightly different ___, so you can often tell where someone comes from.
T1.e: An accent is the way people from a place pronounce words.

T1.q: A person who speaks only one language is m___.
T1.e: Mono- means one: monolingual = speaking one language. Bilingual = two.

T1.q: I don't need help; I can do it by ___ (me).
T1.e: By + reflexive pronoun = alone, without help.

T2.q: We ___ lost on the way to the hotel.
T2.e: Get + past participle describes a change: get lost, get dressed, get married.

T2.q: I need to ___ my car repaired before the trip.
T2.e: Get something done = arrange for someone else to do it for you.

T2.q: She got her brother ___ her with the maths homework.
T2.e: Get + person + to + infinitive = persuade someone to do something.

T2.q: When did you ___ married?
T2.e: After did we use the base form: get married. 'Become married' is not used.

T2.q: It's getting ___; let's go home.
T2.e: Get + adjective = become: it's getting dark/cold/late.

T2.q: My phone ___ (get) stolen while I was on holiday.
T2.e: Get can replace be in passive sentences, especially for bad or unexpected events: it got stolen.

T2.q: Don't let the bad weather get you ___.
T2.e: Get somebody down = make somebody feel sad or depressed.

T2.q: I really must get ___ touch with my old school friends.
T2.e: Get in touch with = contact someone.

T2.q: It takes a while to get the h___ of a new job.
T2.e: Get the hang of something = learn how to do it.

T2.q: The noise from the building site is really getting ___ my nerves.
T2.e: Get on someone's nerves = annoy them.

T2.q: I didn't want to go to the party. ___, I had nothing to wear.
T2.e: Besides adds another reason to support what you just said.

T2.q: We waited for hours, and ___ the bus arrived.
T2.e: At last = finally, after a long wait. At least = the minimum or a positive point.

T2.q: The hotel was very clean; ___, it was right next to the beach.
T2.e: What's more adds another point of the same kind (two positive things).

T2.q: You can't leave now. ___, you promised to help me clean up!
T2.e: After all introduces a reason that the listener should remember or consider.

T2.q: Well, a___, I must go now – it's getting late.
T2.e: Anyway is used to change the subject or end a conversation.

T2.q: The two countries finally signed a peace ___.
T2.e: A treaty is a formal written agreement between countries.

T2.q: The army ___ the town and held it for two months.
T2.e: Capture = take control of a place (or person) by force.

T2.q: Thousands of civilians had to leave their homes and became r___.
T2.e: Refugees are people forced to leave their country because of war or danger.

T2.q: During the war, the city was under s___ for six months, with no food coming in.
T2.e: A siege is when an army surrounds a place so nothing and no one can get in or out.

T2.q: After months of fighting, both sides agreed to a c___ so talks could begin.
T2.e: A ceasefire is an agreement to stop fighting, usually for a period of time.

T3.q: Hardly ___ when the phone rang.
T3.e: After 'hardly' at the start, invert subject and auxiliary: hardly had I… when.

T3.q: Under no circumstances ___ open this door.
T3.e: Negative expressions at the start (under no circumstances) are followed by inversion: should you.

T3.q: Only when I got home ___ that I'd lost my wallet.
T3.e: Only when + clause, then inversion in the main clause: did I realise.

T3.q: Not until the end of the film ___ who the thief was.
T3.e: Not until… at the start is followed by inversion: did we discover.

T3.q: Little ___ (she / know) that her friends were planning a surprise party.
T3.e: Little at the start (= not at all) needs inversion with did: little did she know.

T3.q: No sooner had we arrived ___ it started to rain.
T3.e: No sooner… than (hardly… when). No sooner is a comparative idea, so it takes than.

T3.q: The book is so ___ that I read it in one weekend.
T3.e: Gripping = so exciting that you can't stop reading or watching.

T3.q: The story was completely ___ – nobody could believe it would really happen.
T3.e: Far-fetched = very difficult to believe; unlikely.

T3.q: The main ch___ is a young girl who runs away from home.
T3.e: A character is a person in a book, film or play.

T3.q: The ending was so ___ that half the audience was in tears.
T3.e: Moving = making you feel strong emotions, often sadness.

T3.q: Maria ___ be at home – I've just seen her in town.
T3.e: Can't + infinitive = we're sure something isn't true. Mustn't is for rules, not deduction.

T3.q: They're bound ___ late; they always are.
T3.e: Be bound to + infinitive = certain to happen.

T3.q: I'm not sure where Paolo is. He ___ gone to the gym.
T3.e: May/might have + past participle = it's possible that something happened. 'I'm not sure' shows it's not certain.

T3.q: The ground is wet. It ___ (must / rain) during the night.
T3.e: Must have + past participle for a logical deduction about the past.

T3.q: It's ___ that the match will be cancelled – the forecast is terrible.
T3.e: It's likely that… = it will probably happen. Probably is an adverb, so it can't follow 'it's' like this.

T3.q: The children ___ with laughter at the clown's tricks.
T3.e: Roar with laughter = laugh very loudly.

T3.q: To speak quietly and unclearly, without opening your mouth much, is to ___.
T3.e: Mumble = speak quietly and unclearly. Stammer = repeat sounds because you can't say a word easily.

T3.q: She let out a deep s___ of relief when she heard the good news.
T3.e: A sigh is a long breath out that shows relief, tiredness or sadness.

T3.q: I could hear the gentle h___ of the fridge in the kitchen.
T3.e: A hum is a low, continuous sound, like a machine or a bee.

T3.q: When he's nervous, he repeats the first sound of words; he has a s___.
T3.e: A stammer (or stutter) makes it hard to say words without repeating sounds.

T4.q: The painting is thought ___ over a million euros.
T4.e: Be thought + to + infinitive: is thought to be worth. 'Worth' is an adjective, so it needs 'be'.

T4.q: There ___ to have been a mistake with our order.
T4.e: There seems to be/to have been… is a polite way of not saying something directly.

T4.q: The fire ___ to have started in the kitchen.
T4.e: Passive reporting verb + perfect infinitive: is believed to have started (about the past).

T4.q: It ___ that the new stadium will cost twice as much as planned.
T4.e: It + passive reporting verb + that… distances the writer from the information.

T4.q: The actor is said ___ (live) in a castle in Scotland now.
T4.e: Be said + to + infinitive for the present. The continuous 'to be living' stresses it's happening now.

T4.q: Hurry up! We haven't got all ___!
T4.e: We haven't got all day = we don't have much time, so hurry.

T4.q: Don't worry, you'll get used to it ___ time.
T4.e: In time = eventually, after a period of time.

T4.q: The meeting went on for ___ – nearly four hours!
T4.e: For ages = for a very long time (informal).

T4.q: My grandfather's ideas are a bit behind the t___.
T4.e: Behind the times = old-fashioned.

T4.q: We had a ___ time at the carnival – it was brilliant!
T4.e: Have a whale of a time = enjoy yourself very much.

T4.q: If only I ___ more attention in class last year!
T4.e: If only + past perfect expresses regret about the past.

T4.q: I wish I ___ taller; I'd love to play basketball.
T4.e: Wish + past simple (were) for a present situation you would like to be different.

T4.q: It's high time the government ___ something about unemployment.
T4.e: It's (high) time + past simple = it should happen now. The past form has a present meaning.

T4.q: I'd rather we ___ (stay) at home tonight.
T4.e: Would rather + another subject + past simple for a present or future preference.

T4.q: I wish I ___ (not / say) that to her yesterday – now she's upset.
T4.e: Wish + past perfect for regrets about the past.

T4.q: Twenty euros for a sandwich? That's a complete r___-off!
T4.e: A rip-off = something that costs much more than it should (informal).

T4.q: When her grandmother died, she ___ the house and some money.
T4.e: Inherit = receive money or property from someone after they die.

T4.q: This jacket was a real ___ – only fifteen euros in the sales!
T4.e: A bargain = something bought for less than its usual price.

T4.q: I can't pay you back now. Can I o___ you the money until Friday?
T4.e: Owe = have to pay money back to someone.

T4.q: Many families have to live on a tight ___.
T4.e: Be on a tight budget = have very little money to spend.

T5.q: My boss wants me ___ the report by Friday.
T5.e: Want + object + to + infinitive: wants me to finish.

T5.q: The coach encouraged us ___ harder in the second half.
T5.e: Encourage + object + to + infinitive: encouraged us to play.

T5.q: He's so ___ – he never buys anyone a coffee.
T5.e: Tight-fisted = not willing to spend money (informal).

T5.q: My sister is very e___-going; nothing ever seems to stress her.
T5.e: Easy-going = relaxed and calm, not easily worried or annoyed.

T5.q: If he hadn't missed the bus, he ___ at work now.
T5.e: Mixed conditional: a past condition (hadn't missed) with a present result (would be… now).

T5.q: I'll lend you my bike ___ you bring it back by six.
T5.e: As long as = only if. It introduces a condition.

T5.q: If I ___ (be) you, I'd apologise.
T5.e: Second conditional for advice: If I were you… 'Was' is also possible in informal English.

T5.q: I'm not very good ___ remembering passwords.
T5.e: Good at + noun or -ing.

T5.q: My phone's battery is almost dead – I need to c___ it.
T5.e: Charge a phone/battery = put electricity into it.

T5.q: She's very keen ___ photography and takes pictures everywhere.
T5.e: Keen on = very interested in or enthusiastic about something.

T5.q: You ___ (need / not) have brought a present, but thank you!
T5.e: Needn't have + past participle = you did something, but it wasn't necessary.

T5.q: When I was at school, we ___ wear a uniform; it was compulsory.
T5.e: Had to is the past of must for obligation. Must has no past form.

T5.q: Passengers ___ to leave their bags unattended at the station.
T5.e: Be (not) permitted to + infinitive = be (not) allowed to. Must not and can't have no 'to'.

T5.q: The bus is always late; it's so ___ (reliable).
T5.e: The prefix un- makes an adjective negative: reliable → unreliable.

T5.q: The film was ___ – everyone said it was great, but I thought it was only OK.
T5.e: Overrated = thought to be better than it really is. Over- means too much.

T5.q: This material ___ like silk, but it's actually cotton.
T5.e: Feel like + noun describes how something seems when you touch it. It's not normally continuous here.

T5.q: You ___ as if you haven't slept for days!
T5.e: Look as if/as though + clause = seem, from what we can see.

T5.q: The painter's ___ of her grandmother hangs in the living room.
T5.e: A portrait is a painting or photo of a person.

T5.q: I was g___ with envy when I saw her new car.
T5.e: Green with envy = very jealous.

T5.q: The news came out of the ___ – nobody expected it.
T5.e: Out of the blue = suddenly and unexpectedly.

T6.q: She denied ___ the money.
T6.e: Deny + -ing. The perfect gerund (having taken) stresses that the action was in the past.

T6.q: I'd like ___ to the party, but nobody told me about it.
T6.e: Would like + perfect passive infinitive for a past wish that didn't happen: I'd like to have been invited.

T6.q: He hates ___ what to do by his older brother.
T6.e: Passive gerund (being + past participle): someone tells him what to do, and he hates it.

T6.q: It's no use ___ about it now – it's too late.
T6.e: It's no use + -ing = it's pointless to do something.

T6.q: She seems ___ (lose) her keys again – she's looking everywhere.
T6.e: Seem + perfect infinitive (to have + past participle) for something that probably happened before now.

T6.q: I've ___ my ankle playing football.
T6.e: Sprain = injure a joint (like an ankle or wrist) by twisting it.

T6.q: The doctor gave me a ___ for some antibiotics.
T6.e: A prescription is a doctor's note saying which medicine you need. A recipe is for cooking.

T6.q: Without my glasses I'm as blind as a ___.
T6.e: As blind as a bat = unable to see well. It's a fixed simile.

T6.q: The baby was as good as g___ all through the journey.
T6.e: As good as gold = very well behaved (usually about children).

T6.q: My brother is allergic to nuts, so he always carries his medicine in case he has a bad r___.
T6.e: An allergic reaction is when your body reacts badly to something, like food.

T6.q: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Sardinia.
T6.e: Future continuous (will be + -ing) for an action in progress at a certain time in the future.

T6.q: The Prime Minister is ___ to visit Palermo next month.
T6.e: Be due to + infinitive = be expected or planned for a certain time. 'About to' is for the very near future.

T6.q: By the time you arrive, we ___ dinner.
T6.e: Future perfect (will have + past participle) for an action complete before a future time.

T6.q: Don't call at eight – we ___ the match then.
T6.e: Future continuous: at eight we will be in the middle of watching the match.

T6.q: I'm on the p___ of leaving – can I call you back later?
T6.e: Be on the point of + -ing = be about to do something.

T6.q: We stayed in a small, ___ village where there were hardly any tourists.
T6.e: Unspoilt = still beautiful and natural, not changed by tourism or building.

T6.q: The view from Monte Pellegrino is absolutely ___.
T6.e: Absolutely goes with extreme adjectives like breathtaking (extremely beautiful), not with normal ones.

T6.q: Many tourists come to Sicily to see famous l___s, like the Valley of the Temples.
T6.e: A landmark is a famous building or place that is easy to recognise.

T6.q: The restaurant near the cathedral is a real tourist t___; everything costs twice as much.
T6.e: A tourist trap = a place that attracts tourists and charges them too much.

T6.q: We decided to go ___ the beaten track and explore the small villages in the mountains.
T6.e: Off the beaten track = far from the places most tourists visit.

T7.q: 'Will it rain tomorrow?' 'I hope ___.'
T7.e: I hope not = I hope it won't rain. For positive answers we say I hope so.

T7.q: I don't like horror films, and ___ does my sister.
T7.e: Neither + auxiliary + subject agrees with a negative sentence.

T7.q: I was going to call you, but I forgot ___.
T7.e: We can leave out the verb after 'to' when it's clear: I forgot to (call you).

T7.q: 'Have you been to Malta?' 'No, but I'd like ___.'
T7.e: Would like to: we keep 'to' and leave out the rest (to go to Malta).

T7.q: My brother can swim much faster than I ___.
T7.e: After than/as we can use just the auxiliary instead of repeating the verb: than I can (swim).

T7.q: Rhinos are hunted illegally by ___ for their horns.
T7.e: Poachers hunt or catch animals illegally.

T7.q: The government has created a nature ___ to protect rare birds.
T7.e: A nature reserve is a protected area where animals and plants live safely.

T7.q: A young cat is called a ___.
T7.e: Kitten = young cat. Puppy = young dog, cub = young lion or bear, foal = young horse.

T7.q: Some animals, like bears, h___ during the winter and sleep for months.
T7.e: Hibernate = spend the winter sleeping.

T7.q: Dogs have to be kept on a ___ in the park.
T7.e: A lead is the long strap you use to hold and control a dog when walking. The collar goes round the dog's neck.

T7.q: We need a new ___ for the kitchen.
T7.e: Compound noun: noun + noun, where the first says what type: a coffee machine.

T7.q: I've got two ___ holiday in August.
T7.e: Possessive with time: two weeks' holiday. Weeks is plural, so the apostrophe goes after the -s.

T7.q: I found ___ keys under the sofa.
T7.e: Children is an irregular plural without -s, so we add 's: the children's.

T7.q: The ___ (door / handle) is broken.
T7.e: Compound noun: a door handle, not 'door's handle', because it's a type of handle.

T7.q: My ___ (sister) husband is a chef in Palermo.
T7.e: Possessive 's shows who something or someone belongs to: my sister's husband.

T7.q: ___ the vegetables in a little olive oil for five minutes.
T7.e: Fry = cook in hot oil or fat.

T7.q: Cook the pasta in plenty of ___ salted water.
T7.e: Pasta is cooked in boiling water (water at 100°C).

T7.q: Put the potatoes in the oven and ___ them for an hour.
T7.e: Roast = cook meat or vegetables in an oven, usually with some oil.

T7.q: B___ the cake in a hot oven for forty minutes.
T7.e: Bake = cook bread, cakes etc. in an oven.

T7.q: Make sure you w___ the lettuce carefully before you eat it.
T7.e: Wash vegetables in water to make them clean.

T8.q: That's the café ___ we first met.
T8.e: Where is used in relative clauses for places: the café where we met.

T8.q: My sister, ___ lives in Milan, is coming to visit.
T8.e: Non-defining clause about a person, as subject: who. That can't be used after a comma.

T8.q: He invited twenty friends, most of ___ I'd never met.
T8.e: After a preposition (most of, some of) use whom for people and which for things.

T8.q: The hotel ___ we stayed in was right on the beach.
T8.e: Which (or that) + preposition at the end. 'Where' already includes 'in', so 'where… in' is wrong.

T8.q: The runner, ___ shoe came off during the race, still finished first.
T8.e: Whose shows possession in relative clauses: his shoe → whose shoe.

T8.q: The ___ of the new stadium took three years.
T8.e: After 'the … of' we need a noun: construction (-ion ending).

T8.q: We need to ___ the rules so everyone understands them.
T8.e: The suffix -ify makes verbs from adjectives: simple → simplify.

T8.q: The ___ of the sea here is over two hundred metres.
T8.e: Depth is the noun from deep, like length from long and width from wide.

T8.q: Her ___ (perform) in the final was outstanding.
T8.e: The noun from perform is performance (-ance ending).

T8.q: Practice will ___ (sharp) your skills.
T8.e: The suffix -en makes verbs from adjectives: sharp → sharpen, wide → widen.

T8.q: ___ I love about Sicily is the food.
T8.e: Cleft sentence: What + clause + is… puts the focus on the last part (the food).

T8.q: It was my grandmother ___ taught me to cook.
T8.e: It + be + person + who… emphasises the person.

T8.q: All I want ___ a quiet weekend at home.
T8.e: All (= the only thing) + clause + is. It works like 'What I want is…'.

T8.q: The reason ___ I called is to invite you to dinner.
T8.e: The reason why… is… is a way of focusing on the explanation.

T8.q: What I did next ___ (be) phone the police.
T8.e: What + do clause + be + infinitive: What I did was phone… It's past, so use was.

T8.q: I ___ my umbrella at home, so I got wet.
T8.e: Leave something + a place. We don't use forget with a place: I forgot my umbrella, I left it at home.

T8.q: Can you r___ me to call my grandmother later?
T8.e: Remind someone to do something = help them remember. Remember is what you do yourself.

T8.q: The price of houses has ___ a lot in the last few years.
T8.e: Rise (rose, risen) has no object: prices rise. Raise needs an object: raise prices.

T8.q: Can I b___ your pen? I'll give it back in a minute.
T8.e: Borrow = take something that you will give back. Lend = give it to someone for a time.

T8.q: It's ___ to swim here when the red flag is flying.
T8.e: Unsafe = dangerous. Insecure is about feeling not confident, unsure = not certain.
